Land and Water Conservation Fund - General Information


2026 LWCF Grant Round is now closed.

The Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 established a federal reimbursement program for the acquisition and/or development of public outdoor recreation areas. The Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) is administered in Virginia by the Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) on behalf of the National Park Service (NPS). The program represents a federal, state and local partnership. A key feature of the program is that all LWCF assisted areas must be maintained and opened, in perpetuity, as public outdoor recreation areas. This requirement ensures their use for future generations.

Virginia has received more than $135 million in assistance since the LWCF began. It has made more than 430 projects possible within the Commonwealth.

The LWCF is a 50-50% matching reimbursement program. The grant recipient must be able to fund 100% of the project while seeking periodic reimbursements.

For further details about NPS LWCF program guidelines and project eligibility, please review the newly released version of the National Park Service LWCF Manual V2026  at https://www.nps.gov/subjects/lwcf/v2026.htm

**Version 72.1 is no longer effective as of May 1, 2026**

Please see Chapter 3 for project eligibility and Chapter 4 for proposal development and review requirements.

For specific regulatory requirements please refer to Federal Regulations: 2 C.F.R. § 200, 2 C.F.R. § 1402, 36 CFR 59.

 

LWCF State & Local Assistance Grant

The 2026 Land & Water Conservation Fund State & Local Assistance (LWCF) Virginia DCR Grant Round is now closed. LWCF is federal funding as a 50/50% matching reimbursement grant program for eligible projects.  The 2027 DCR LWCF Grant Round is contingent upon available federal apportionment.

This recording and presentation was for the 2026 Grant Round. Some requirements may change but this can be referenced for general information.

A virtual workshop for potential applicants for the now closed 2026 LWCF Grant Round was held Tuesday, July 14, 2026.

View the recording

Download the PowerPoint presentation.

Entities eligible to compete for LWCF funding

  • Counties, cities and towns
  • Park and recreation authorities
  • Tribes
  • State agencies

Grant Application Documents:

Please see the following documents and forms from the 2026 LWCF Grant Round. The manual and forms are for reference only. The application, budget and timeline documents may be updated for future grant rounds.

  • LWCF 2026 DCR Grant Round Manual **read first prior to completing application **
  • DCR Preapplication
  • Project Budget Worksheet and Narrative
  • Project Timeline
  • How to Reference the VOP
  • Maps and Property Documents Guidance
  • LWCF 2026 Scoring Criteria
  • Preapplication Environmental Guidance document
  • Additional documents and procedures: 
    These procedures may change in future grant rounds and this is for informational purposes only.
    • New in 2026: it is not required to have proof of correspondence with reviewing agencies during the application phase. PRR Grant Staff will lead selected project sponsors through a series of virtual meetings to cover all the required procedures for successful NEPA and Section 106 compliance and NPS submission.
    • This Compliance Phase Environmental Guidance document provides information about these procedures and should be referenced if providing any of the optional environmental information listed in the preapplication document.
    • Be prepared: The time period from application to official grant award is typically approximately one year. Project agreements and grant awards from the 2026 grant round are expected August of 2027. No demolition, construction, or transfer of acquisition can take place until grant award is in hand.
    • You may reference the links provided in the VOP Section 4.3 to determine appropriate review procedures and timelines for the different agencies. The recommended first step is to run “NEPA Assist” to get a simplified report of any potential concerns on or near the property. It is important to be aware that Section 106 surveys may be conducted – as determined by VDHR. Permitting, especially in wetlands and waterways, may take additional time as well as determined by multiple agencies.
  • Please refer to Open Project Selection Process (OPSP) 2025-2030 for further information about the LWCF Grant Round general procedures and definitions.

All projects must go through full NEPA and Section 106 review prior to submission to the National Park Service. NPS has the authority to approve compliance or ask for further information.

Please note that some projects will not be simple Categorical Exclusions. Also, projects may need further Virginia State Review Procedures and local review, as applicable, depending on project scope and design.

  • The National Park Service requires every state has a NPS approved State Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan to remain eligible for LWCF Funding. Virginia's State Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP) is the Virginia Outdoors Plan

Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership Program (ORLP)

The Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership (ORLP) Program is a subprogram of LWCF and provides 50-50% matching reimbursement grants for the acquisition, development, and rehabilitation of parks in qualifying urban and tribal areas. Information on DCR preapplication processes for the national competition can be found at https://www.dcr.virginia.gov/recreational-planning/orlp.

Readiness and Recreation Initiative (RARI) Program

The National Park Service has announced the Readiness and Recreation Initiative (RARI) national program opportunity.  This NPS opportunity will be a rolling application program for the next 5 years. DCR will prepare documents for an open grant round tentative early winter 2026. 

These grant funds have been available nationally through the federal National Park Service Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) combined with the Department of Defense (DOD) Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program. This grant purpose protects the Nation’s military readiness, enhances relationships with communities, preserves the environment, and improves military installation and community resilience to climate change.

These projects are specifically for acquisitions within Virginia’s Potomac or Tidewater Sentinel Landscapes https://sentinellandscapes.org/ and must be coordinated with adjacent/nearby military installations.

Please also contact the Department of Forestry REPI office for further information and coordination. https://dof.virginia.gov/land-water-protection/farm-and-forestland-conservation/virginia-security-corridor/

Potential LWCF Conversions

All parks that have received funding from the LWCF State and Local Assistance Grant Program must maintain public outdoor recreation use in perpetuity. If your locality or agency is proposing or being presented with any non-outdoor recreation development or significant use changes on LWCF protected parks, please email contact@example.virginia.gov or mail information to:
